headline: BBC staff have questioned Director-General Matt Brittin at a town hall over his praise for an AI-generated episode of Doctor Who.
score_reason: Lowered by one: the town hall was on 7 Oct 2026, before the window, and the story is workplace debate rather than a decision.
importance_line: BBC staff and creative workers in the UK regions worry about generative AI replacing human-made programmes, while Brittin says humans lead; no change in policy has been announced.
summary: Deadline reports that at a BBC staff town hall on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, employees answered Director-General Matt Brittin's earlier remark, made last week at the Royal Television Society London Convention and covered in national newspapers, that an AI-generated Doctor Who episode was "pretty good", and asked him to rethink his interest in AI-made programmes. Brittin replied that he was making a point about the pace of change, that "humans are leading", and that the BBC must understand AI's risks to its journalistic integrity.
notes: Reply story: names the earlier remark (Brittin at the RTS London Convention the previous week). Not previously carried by this desk.
